newsitem.title: UK: STOCKS -- Closing stock market indices, May 20.
newsitem.headline: STOCKS -- Closing stock market indices, May 20.

text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Tuesday.

LONDON - The threat of higher U.S. interest rates sent UK shares lower for the second day running, amid concern that fiscal policy may be tightened in Britain as early as next month. The FTSE 100 leading share index closed, which dropped nearly 50 points on Monday, ended 37.7 points down at 4,607.5.

FRANKFURT - German shares closed bourse trade down on Tuesday as dealers remained cautious ahead of today's meeting of the Federal Reserve, with the main market feature being drug group BASF's lawsuit woes. The DAX-30 blue-chip index closed trade 61.12 points lower at 3,543.43. In post-bourse trade the index fell 53.06 to 3,516.20.

PARIS - French shares finished more than one percent lower on Tuesday as investors took profits on last week's rise of over five percent. Traders said weakness in bonds and the dollar ahead of the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting today also encouraged sellers. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 33.17 points at 2,751.11.

ZURICH - After a string of record closes last week, shares ended more than one percent lower, dragged down by losses in index-heavyweight shares. Dealers said Wall Street's early weakness and the fall in the dollar put blue-chip stocks such as Novartis, Roche and Nestle under pressure. The blue-chip SMI slid 76.5 points, or 1.48 percent, to 5,081.0 and the all-share SPI was down 41.63 points to 3,214.28 points.

TOKYO - Stocks slipped on Tuesday afternoon, weighed on by damage to exporter issues from the yen's strength against the dollar, brokers said. News that prosecutors had raided Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd in a widening investigation into links between financial firms and racketeers also hurt sentiment, they said. The Nikkei average fell 156.92 points to close at 20,332.83.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index surged to new record highs on Tuesday as increased buying on HSBC Holdings and property stocks in the afternoon carried the index to its third record close in eight sessions, brokers said. The Hang Seng ended up 127.38 points at a closing record of 14,236.20, after hitting an all-time intra-day high of 14,253.97 in late trade.

SYDNEY - Australian stocks ended barely changed on Tuesday with all eyes on the U.S. as traders waited to assess any rate implications of the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting later today. The All Ordinaries Index shed a wafer-thin 0.3 points to 2,530.7.

JOHANNESBURG - South African shares ended down as fears of a United States interest rate rise swept global markets and knocked industrial shares firmly into negative territory, dealers said on Tuesday. However, the golds index performed stronger, taking heart from a rally in the international bullion price that saw the local sector claw back more than half of Monday's steep losses. The U.S. Federal Reserve is meeting to discuss whether a further rate rise is necessary to curb inflation fears in the country's booming economy.

Economic analysts are split as to the likelihood of a rise, but European equity markets and Wall Street shares headed downwards in the afternoon in anticipation of a hike and the South African market joined them. The all-share index dropped 10.4 points to 7,106.2 as the industrial index dipped 26.5 points to 8,372.0. The golds index climbed 20.3 points to 1,213.1.
